Skills Targeted Python environment | LLM fundamentals | Tokens & context | API integration | Git workflow Tools & Stack Python 3.11+ | VS Code | Git / GitHub | venv | Anthropic or OpenAI SDK | python-dotenv T A S K L I S T 01 Set up a professional dev environment Install Python 3.11 or newer, VS Code with the Python extension, and Git. Create a virtual environment and a requirements.txt. Never install packages globally. Create the GitHub repo vaultx-ai-internship with a README and a proper .gitignore. Make at least five meaningful commits this week. One giant commit at the end scores zero. 02 Build the vocabulary Write clear definitions in your own words for: token, context window, temperature, top-p, system prompt, embedding, hallucination, fine-tuning, inference. Explain the difference between a base model and an instruction-tuned model. Explain in three sentences why an LLM predicts text rather than "knows" facts. 03 Make your first API ca

-tuning, inference. Explain the difference between a base model and an instruction-tuned model. Explain in three sentences why an LLM predicts text rather than "knows" facts. 03 Make your first API call Get an API key and store it in .env. Load it with python-dotenv. Write a script that sends a prompt and prints the response. Print the token usage from the response object and calculate the cost of that single call. 04 Experiment with generation parameters Run the same prompt at temperature 0, 0.7 and 1.0, three times each. Record the outputs in a table and describe how variance changes. State which temperature you would choose for: a support bot, a code generator, and a marketing copy tool. Justify each. 05 Build a reusable API wrapper Write a Python class or module that handles: sending messages, retry on failure, timeout, and token counting. Add proper error handling for rate limits and invalid keys. It must never crash on a bad response. You will reuse this module for the next seven

Skills Targeted Prompt patterns | System prompts | JSON / schema output | Few-shot | Prompt evaluation Tools & Stack Anthropic / OpenAI SDK | Pydantic | JSON schema | your Week-01 API wrapper T A S K L I S T 01 Master the core prompt patterns Build a reusable template library covering zero-shot, few-shot, role/system, chain-of-thought and constrained output. 02 Force structured output Make the model return strict JSON that matches a Pydantic schema. Validate the response and auto-retry when the JSON is invalid. 03 Build a classification tool Given an input (e.g. a support message), output {category, priority, sentiment, needs_human} as validated JSON. Test it on 20 realistic samples. 04 Build an extraction tool Extract structured fields from messy text (invoices, emails) into JSON. Handle missing fields gracefully instead of crashing. 05 Evaluate your prompts Build a tiny eval set (10–20 cases) with expected outputs. Measure accuracy, iterate the prompt, and record the impr

Connect at least two real apps you use (e.g. Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, Notion) via official connectors. 02 Automation #1 — inbox / message triage Trigger on a new email / form / message → LLM classifies + summarises → route (label, Slack ping, or Sheet row). It must run automatically, not on a manual button. 03 Add a structured LLM step Use your Week-02 JSON prompting inside the workflow so the LLM output reliably drives branching (priority = high → notify). 04 Handle failures Add error branches, retries and a fallback so the workflow never breaks silently. Log every run. 05 Automation #2 — content / data pipeline New row / RSS / upload → LLM transforms (summary, tags, draft)

ing | Embeddings | Vector DB | Retrieval | Grounded generation | Citations Tools & Stack Anthropic / OpenAI embeddings | Chroma / FAISS / pgvector | LangChain or plain Python | a real document set T A S K L I S T 01 Ingest a real corpus Take a real document set (company docs, PDFs, a knowledge base). Clean and chunk it sensibly (size + overlap) and explain your chunking choices. 02 Build the index Embed the chunks and store them in a vector DB (Chroma / FAISS / pgvector). Persist the index so it survives a restart. 03 Retrieval + grounded answers Given a question, retrieve top-k chunks and answer ONLY from them, with citations to the source chunks. Refuse when the answer isn't in the documents. 04 Evaluate honestly Build 15–20 QA pairs; measure how often answers are correct and grounded.
